report:
Conclusion: The difference vector (B − A) encodes a cooking/culinary bias — it pushes residual activations toward kitchen/recipe/food words.

Why I believe this
- Spatial pattern: the difference norm is concentrated in middle-to-late layers (roughly layers 14–25, especially positions 0–1), i.e. where higher-level lexical/conceptual features are normally represented.
- Logit‑lens vocabulary: the high‑norm (layer,position) cells consistently point at cooking-related tokens across many of those layers and positions: "Kitchen", "Cook", "Cooking", "recipes", "Bake", "Baked", "butter", "cake", "Chef", "culinary", "Thanksgiving", "vanilla", etc. These tokens recur across layers 17–25 (and earlier layers to a lesser extent).
- The signal is therefore coherent and domain‑specific (culinary/recipes) rather than random/noisy: many different cells all point toward related tokens.

Caveats
- Some earlier/other cells show unrelated tokens (e.g. "landscape", numbers, names), but the dominant, repeated theme across the highest‑norm cells is culinary vocabulary.
- I cannot say from this evidence whether B was fine‑tuned on cooking text, or whether the difference arises from another training/architecture change — only that B activations systematically push toward cooking/recipe tokens relative to A.
